audit_findings.title: Owner-earnings numerator and fully exchanged share denominator represent different claims
audit_findings.magnitude: 23.2% noncontrolling economic interest at 2026-06-30; a computed pro-rata correction would raise base value from $34.67 to approximately $44.42 per share and bull value from $40.47 to approximately $51.97
audit_findings.mechanism: The numerator omits some earnings attributable to exchangeable-unit holders while the 470.066893 million fully diluted denominator includes their securities, understating OE per share.
audit_findings.evidence: Accordingly, the numerator is also adjusted to include the earnings (loss) allocated to the holders of noncontrolling interests.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim-basis error is demonstrated. A conservative pro-rata sensitivity using the filed 23.2% noncontrolling interest materially raises the numerical valuation, but even the resulting bull value remains approximately 35% below the $80.17 market price and cannot reverse the no-buy conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild all historical OE components on a consolidated basis including noncontrolling interests and rerun the anchor and scenarios using the existing fully exchanged denominator; alternatively, rerun parent-attributable OE with the corresponding parent-share denominator.

audit_findings.title: Temporary hedge benefits may be capitalized as perpetual owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $193 million of 2025 benefits ($103 million interest-rate swaps plus $90 million cross-currency swaps); full removal from the anchor would reduce computed base value by approximately $5.77 per share and bull value by approximately $6.80 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Hedge benefits reduce retained interest expense in equity-level OE; projecting them after contract expiry overstates recurring OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Amount includes a benefit of $ 103 million, $ 135 million, and $ 83 million during 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively, related to our interest rate swaps.
audit_findings.explanation: The benefits are filed and are large relative to the $1,079.4 million anchor, but correcting them can only lower an already sub-market valuation. An extreme sensitivity removing all $193 million lowers base value to about $28.90 and bull value to about $33.67 versus the $80.17 price, so it cannot reverse the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Map interest-rate and cross-currency benefits into every OE year, determine sustainable post-expiry financing costs and replacement-hedge terms, and rerun the existing scenarios with normalized interest expense.

audit_findings.title: A derivative liability may be an omitted claim ahead of equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $128 million net derivative liability at 2026-06-30 ($175 million liabilities less $47 million assets), equal to approximately $0.27 per diluted share and 0.8% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any derivative settlement not already reflected in projected financing or foreign-exchange cash flows would require a bridge deduction ahead of equity.
audit_findings.evidence: The net fair value of these derivative instruments was a liability of $290 million as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing resolves the balance-sheet amount. Even deducting the entire $128 million net liability would reduce base value only from $34.67 to about $34.40 per share, far too little to affect the conclusion. Whether a deduction is conceptually appropriate remains subject to avoiding double counting, but its maximum filed scale is not material here.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 2026 derivative assets and liabilities by contract to forecast settlements and OE cash flows; deduct only settlements not already represented in OE.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter ruling ignores the planned Carrols refranchising transition
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed RH figures include $44 million of 2025 adjusted operating income and $145 million of 2025 capital expenditures, versus $16 million and $37 million respectively for the first half of 2026, with 994 Carrols Burger King Company restaurants remaining at 2026-06-30
audit_findings.mechanism: Refranchising changes restaurant OE, royalty income, maintenance and remodel capital, working capital, taxes, sale proceeds, and the steady-state operating perimeter used for the anchor and growth forecast.
audit_findings.evidence: A key component of our portfolio acquisitions in recent years, including the Carrols Acquisition, was to improve, remodel, and refranchise the vast majority of these restaurants over the coming years to new and existing franchisees.
audit_findings.explanation: The non-null transition is demonstrated, but the supplied record does not establish its net value effect because lower restaurant earnings and capital needs must be weighed against royalties and after-tax sale proceeds. The $145 million 2025 RH capital expenditure is 13.4% of anchor OE, so the issue cannot be dismissed, yet no complete transition schedule establishes that it is material to the final conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Build and rerun a restaurant-level transition schedule covering remodel timing and spending, refranchising dates, lost restaurant OE, replacement royalties, sale proceeds, taxes, working-capital release, and the steady-state perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Recurring refinancing costs may fall outside an operating-cash-flow-derived OE measure
audit_findings.magnitude: $41 million paid in 2024 and $44 million in 2023; treating the larger amount as an annual recurring cost would reduce computed base value by approximately $1.32 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Deferred financing-cost amortization is added back in operating cash flow while the original cash fees are classified in financing activities, causing an OCF-derived OE measure to omit refinancing cash costs.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2024, we incurred aggregate deferred financing costs of $ 41 million in connection with the First 2024 Amendment, the Second 2024 Amendment, the issuance of the 6.125 % First Lien Senior Notes due 2029 and the issuance of the 5.625 % First Lien Senior Notes due 2029.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash-flow classification gap is demonstrated. The larger filed annual fee is 4.1% of anchor OE and, even if deducted every year rather than only during refinancing cycles, would lower base value only to about $33.35 per share versus the $80.17 market price. It therefore cannot change the current conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to deferred-financing-cost amortization and financing-activity cash fees, derive a cycle-normalized annual cost consistent with the 2028–2030 maturity schedule, and rerun the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: An unreserved historical tax claim could sit outside modeled owner earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: An adverse CRA settlement, interest, or penalties would reduce equity value through a one-time bridge claim or future OE cash outflow because no provision is recorded.
audit_findings.evidence: We believe that our tax position with respect to this matter is appropriate, and thus we have not made any provisions in our financial statements with respect to this matter.
audit_findings.explanation: The existing dispute and absence of a reserve are demonstrated, but the filing does not disclose the disputed deductions, asserted tax, interest, penalties, or a loss range. The broader $88 million of recorded unrecognized tax benefits and related amounts cannot be assigned to this separate unreserved matter, so the record cannot establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the CRA assessment or audit correspondence, disputed deduction and tax amounts, accrued interest and penalties, counsel's probability analysis, and developments through June 2026; then apply the probability-weighted after-tax claim in the bridge or modeled cash flows without double counting.
